title: Onboarding eval: latency-cost sensitivity sweep
content:
Purpose:
Run a set of latency/cost vs. quality sensitivity sweeps to inform safe default knobs for model onboarding (hosted + dedicated). Focus: batching, KV/prefix caching, and max_tokens caps for interactive QA/chat workloads.

Background summary:
- Model under test: rw-infer/llamaX-13b (fp16 baseline) and quantized int8-lite variant used for cheaper capacity slots.
- Onboarding goal: choose defaults that avoid noticeable quality regressions while maximizing throughput and lowering per-token cost.
- Previous quick sweep (internal) showed batch sizes >8 degrade p95 for single-turn chats on 32k sequence workloads; this doc records a systematic sweep and recommended heuristics.

Experiment design:
- Workloads: 3 promptsets representative of shipped customers: (1) Short chat (avg prompt 40 tokens), (2) Multi-turn QA (avg prompt 120 tokens with 1 prior turn), (3) Long-instruction summarization (avg prompt 600 tokens).
- Swept parameters: batch_size = [1,2,4,8,16]; cache = [off, prefix-kv-on]; max_tokens_cap = [64,128,256,512]. Also compared fp16 vs int8-lite.
- Routing: single-region NVidia A100 40GB pool (hosted) for baseline; Dedicated pool simulated with identical hardware but with reserved capacity throttling enabled.
- Metrics collected per config: p50 latency (ms), p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec (effective), cost_per_1M_tokens (USD, infra + model), QA-F1 (for QA promptset), Rouge-L (for summarization), token-quality-delta (relative to fp16 baseline). Also record cache_hit_rate and batch_queue_wait_ms.
- Run size: 10k requests per promptset per config. Warmup: 500 requests before measurement.

Key numeric results (high level):
- Short chat (avg 40 tokens) fp16:
  - batch 1, cache on, max_tokens=128: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, tokens/sec=950, cost/1M=$18.
  - batch 8, cache on, max_tokens=128: p50=70ms, p95=210ms, tokens/sec=4200, cost/1M=$5.2.
  - batch 16, cache off, max_tokens=256: p95 shoots to ~480ms and user-observable latency increases; quality unchanged.

- Multi-turn QA (avg 120 tokens) fp16:
  - cache off, batch1, max_tokens=256: p95=520ms, QA-F1=0.78, cost/1M=$55.
  - cache on, batch4, max_tokens=256: p95=310ms, QA-F1=0.77 (-0.01), cost/1M=$17.5, cache_hit_rate=0.64.
  - int8-lite, cache on, batch4: QA-F1=0.73 (-0.05 vs fp16), p95=290ms, cost/1M=$11.2.

- Summarization (avg 600 tokens) fp16:
  - batch1, cache irrelevant, max_tokens=512: p95=1.9s, Rouge-L=0.62.
  - batch2: p95=2.1s, throughput improves slightly; cost/1M drops from $220 to $180. Quality unchanged.

Observations and tradeoffs:
1) Batching gives large cost reductions for short-turn workloads (short chat) without quality loss, but increases queueing latency which affects p95. For interactive apps, prefer small-to-moderate batches (2-8) depending on SLO.
2) Prefix/KV caching yields the biggest latency improvement for multi-turn QA (p95 down ~40%) and massive cost improvements because repeated context avoids recomputation. Cache hit rates vary by promptset; highest for chat and QA (~0.6-0.8), negligible for one-off summarization.
3) max_tokens cap is a linear cost lever: raising cap from 128->512 multiplies worst-case cost. For interactive defaults, 256 is a pragmatic upper bound; allow overrides on a per-route basis.
4) Quantized int8 variant provides ~30-45% cost savings at the price of measurable quality drop for sensitive QA tasks (QA-F1 -0.03 to -0.06). Int8 is acceptable for non-critical summarization and high-throughput embedding-like workloads.
5) p95 tail is dominated by batching queue wait + long generation times for long outputs. Autoscaling and burst capacity reduce p95 but add cost; prefer fallback model variants for tail resilience.

Default onboarding heuristics (recommended):
- Interactive chat routes: default batch_size=4, cache=on (prefix), max_tokens_cap=256, prefer fp16 baseline; if cost pressure and non-critical quality, opt-in int8-lite with explicit QA regen checks.
- QA-heavy routes (multi-turn): cache=on mandatory; batch_size=2-4 depending on SLO; maintain max_tokens_cap=256; run a small promptset regression (500 queries) before promoting any quantized variant.
- Batch/async summarization: batch_size up to 16 or use dedicated bulk queue; max_tokens_cap set per-job (allow 512+), use int8-lite as default for cost-sensitive pipelines.

Regression detection & onboarding checklist (for new model variants):
- Always run the standardized promptset (short-chat, multi-turn QA, summarization) with the target quantization and the recommended default knobs.
- Thresholds to fail onboarding: QA-F1 drop >0.03 absolute on QA promptset OR Rouge-L drop >0.02 on summarization OR p95 increase >20% for interactive routes.
- If any threshold fails, run focused ack-regression tests: top-N failing prompts, human review of 100 examples, and rollback to fp16.

Action items / next steps:
- (Jordan) Add these heuristics to the onboarding runbook and create automated gating in the CI harness (JIRA-ENG-2041).
- (Ravi) Implement a small smoke-test that runs at model-promote time: 1k queries across promptsets, returns pass/fail and perf/cost deltas.
- (Elena) Add int8-lite-specific quality checks to the eval dashboard and annotate model variants with recommended route tags.
- Schedule: aim to integrate into the onboarding pipeline by end of Q2 2026.

Open questions / notes:
- Need to validate these heuristics on dedicated pools using the exact customer autoscaling profiles; reserved capacity can change queueing dynamics.
- Explore dynamic batching caps: allow batch to grow but set a latency budget that preempts batch growth when target p95 exceeds SLO. Prototype idea: adaptive batch limiter based on recent p95 window.
- Investigate hybrid routing that uses int8-lite for tail/backfill traffic and fp16 for latency-sensitive sampled requests.
